Memorylessness makes the Bellman value b_k=max_h(g_r(h)+e^(-r h)b_(k-1)); derivative has one positive root for b<1, yielding the stated unique recurrence and reverse-index optimal gaps. b_k grows to 1 and epsilon_(k+1)=epsilon_k-(r/2)epsilon_k^2+O(epsilon^3) yields n epsilon_n->2/r; sum of gap asymptotics yields terminal time. For equal gaps H_r(h)=g_r(h)/(1-e^(-r h))=1-h/2+O(h^2); comparison of e^(-rnh) and h/2 produces sharp miss ~log n/(2rn). Independent numerical recurrence and direct first-detection probability summation match across r=.5,1,2,3 and n=1,2,4,6, including r=2 n=6 b=6/7. Explicit no-horizon, one irreversible episode and no imperfect detection boundary.
